objectives.model-session-state: Distinguish browser-held session identifiers from server-held authentication state.
objectives.trace-session-lifecycle: Trace session creation, lookup, expiry and logout through a Java servlet application.
objectives.design-session-storage: Explain how multiple application instances share session state and handle missing or unavailable state.
objectives.protect-session-credentials: Choose session identifier rotation, storage controls and cookie attributes for their distinct security purposes.

practice.prompt: A valid browser cookie reaches node B after sign-in on node A. B reports a missing session, while A still loads the account. Both nodes report healthy process-local stores. What should you inspect first?

choices.label: Where the authenticated session was stored and whether B can read that same record.
choices.reason: The same cookie reaches both nodes and only A finds state. Compare repository ownership and routing before changing security settings.

choices.label: Whether Secure prevented the browser from sending its cookie.
choices.reason: B already received the cookie. Browser delivery cannot explain why only A has a matching record.

choices.label: Whether idle expiry is too short on both nodes.
choices.reason: A still finds the record. A shared expiry problem does not explain the node-specific result.

topics.sourceLabel: Horizontal scaling and shared session storage

browser-and-server.title: Two pieces of one authenticated session

items.label: Browser cookie store
items.detail: Keeps the opaque identifier and applies storage and send rules.

items.label: HTTP request
items.detail: Sends the cookie name and value when the rules allow it.

items.label: Session repository
items.detail: Associates an identifier with stored state and lifecycle information.

items.label: Request security context
items.detail: A configured repository restores authentication for this request. Authorization still evaluates the requested action.

follow-a-session.title: Inspect one session across four requests

groups.title: An operator signs in, reads a roster, then signs out

items.label: Visit the login form
items.detail: A pre-login session can carry form state. Its mere existence does not establish a signed-in operator.

items.label: Submit accepted evidence
items.detail: The configured login establishes authentication. It changes the identifier of an existing session and saves the context for later use.

items.label: Read the roster
items.detail: The next request presents the current identifier. The session is valid and the restored authentication is sent to the roster’s authorization decision.

items.label: Confirm logout
items.detail: The logout handler invalidates the server session and clears authentication. A later request cannot restore the retired context from that identifier.

where-the-record-lives.title: Both application nodes use one session repository

items.label: Sign in on A
items.detail: A saves the authenticated session record under its current identifier.

items.label: Shared store
items.detail: The repository owns availability, expiry and invalidation of the shared record.

items.label: Next request on B
items.detail: B receives the same cookie and asks the repository for the record.

items.label: Authorization
items.detail: B applies the requested action’s policy after restoring valid authentication.
